top_story.headline: FBI Director Kash Patel amends his stock report to add a six-figure MicroStrategy purchase he left off
top_story.dek: The amendment, delivered to Mark Alfred's OGE inbox on Nov. 5, discloses a purchase about 186 days after it happened, against the STOCK Act's 45-day limit.
paragraphs: A Justice Department cover letter dated May 28, 2026 forwards a May 26 request from Kashyap P. Patel, Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, to amend his periodic transaction report (278-T). The original was signed December 4, 2025 and certified by the U.S. Office of Government Ethics on December 30, 2025. The amendment adds a purchase of MicroStrategy, Inc (MSTR) on November 21, 2025, in the $100,001-$250,000 range. Patel says it was inadvertently omitted because of a miscommunication.

The original report lists only one sale: ON Semiconductor Corporation (ON) on October 6, 2025, for $50,001-$100,000. The MicroStrategy purchase was not reported until the May 26, 2026 amendment, about 186 days after the trade. That is a late disclosure. The amendment came roughly six months after OGE certified the original. The report also notes that Patel received a 30-day filing extension.

The document arrived Nov. 5 at oge@markalfred.news in answer to an automatically filed OGE Form 201 request. Also delivered the same day was a certificate of divestiture for Todd Blanche (file OGE-2026-183-CDIV); the readable text did not give his position.

Todd Blanche (Not stated in the readable text): Certificate of divestiture. Arrived Nov 5. The file 'Blanche, Todd OGE-2026-183-CDIV.pdf' (1149421 bytes) is a certificate of divestiture under section 1043 of the Internal Revenue Code. The readable text is mostly standard language; the certificate number, issuance date, eligible person fields and the asset table (quantity and asset) are blank or unreadable. The attachment is signed by Scott A. de la Vega, Ethics Counsel. What was divested could not be determined from the text. OGE collection.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.
